label: The Acts of Onesiphorus places a Christian community at Parium in Mysia

date.note: No internal date. Harnack lists Parium among the towns attested between Trajan (acc. 98) and the death of Marcus Aurelius (180); the range is that bracket, not a dating of the apocryphal Acts themselves, whose composition is later and uncertain.

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, p. 188; synopsis at p. 95

notes: The weakest item in the batch, graded hagiographic because it rests on legendary apocryphal Acts. Harnack himself hedges: 'Parium in Mysia (for in this connection we may trust the Acta Onesiphori)' (p. 188), cross-referring to Acta SS. Feb. II p. 42. Recorded because Harnack counts it among his fourteen towns; the grade keeps it from being silently promoted alongside the contemporary attestations. Parium (511354) is the Propontic city in Mysia, not Parion Oros, the Cilician mountain (658566).
